candidates.attacker_control: HTTP query/form parameters handled by ValidatorBase content negotiation: ?lang= and ?langtag= (LangTagValidatorHTML.executeHTML), ?iri= (IRIValidatorHTML.executeHTML, including repeated values), ?query= (QueryValidatorHTML.executeHTML) and ?update= (UpdateValidatorHTML.executeHTML), plus the parser/validation error text that echoes those strings. FMod_UI registers these servlets at /$/validate/langtag, /$/validate/iri, /$/validate/query, /$/validate/update.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the raw query/update text in the 'Input' block is encoded via ValidatorHtmlLib.output()/htmlQuote, so the flaw is confined to direct echoes and exception-message paths. Checked DataValidatorHTML, which does apply htmlQuote to parser messages (showing the intended pattern). Checked that the default jena-fuseki-main resources shiro.ini maps /$/** to localhostFilter and that FMod_Admin/FusekiServerCtl install this default, which limits default remote reachability (but the shipped file also documents /$/** = anon and reverse proxies erase the distinction). Checked ServletOps error paths are text/plain (not an XSS sink).
candidates.impact: Script execution in the Fuseki origin when a user (e.g., an administrator using the local UI) opens the crafted validator URL. Because the script runs same-origin, it can issue requests to the Fuseki admin API (/$/datasets create/delete, /$/backup, /$/server, stats) with the victim's network position/credentials, exfiltrate data, or modify datasets; it can also read non-HttpOnly data in the origin. Severity is bounded by the loopback-only default configuration but is materially higher where /$/** is exposed or the server sits behind a local reverse proxy.
candidates.prerequisites: A victim able to reach the Fuseki /$/validate/* endpoints must follow an attacker-supplied link (or an attacker must be able to submit the request with a victim's browser). In the stock distribution, FMod_Shiro installs shiro.ini whose default maps /$/** to localhostFilter, so the endpoints are loopback-restricted unless the operator has opened /$/** (a documented option in the shipped shiro.ini) or the server is behind a reverse proxy so requests appear to come from localhost.
candidates.root_cause: The Fuseki HTML validation servlets emit attacker-supplied request parameters and raw parser/validator exception messages into a text/html response without HTML-encoding. ValidatorHtmlLib.htmlQuote/htmlQuote-based output() exists and is used for the parsed input in Query/Update validators, but it is not applied to the direct echoes of ?lang=/?langtag=/?iri= nor to parser error messages. QueryValidatorHTML/UpdateValidatorHTML catch parse failures and call ServletOutputStream.println(ex.getMessage()) directly; JavaCC messages embed the offending token image, and Jena LangTag/IRI exception messages embed the offending string, so attacker-chosen markup is reflected.
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in Fuseki HTML validation endpoints ($/validate/query|update|iri|langtag)
candidates.trace: Request -> ValidatorBase -> LangTagValidatorHTML.executeHTML/IRIValidatorHTML.executeHTML/QueryValidatorHTML.executeHTML/UpdateValidatorHTML.executeHTML -> ValidatorHtmlLib.setHeaders sets Content-Type text/html -> outStream.println(languageTag) / System.out.println(iriStr) / outStream.println(ex.getMessage()) writes unencoded attacker-controlled text -> browser parses response as HTML and executes injected script in the Fuseki origin.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Whether a specific JavaCC/Jena parse-error message always contains enough attacker-controlled markup to form a working payload was not executed/verified; the direct raw echoes in LangTagValidatorHTML/IRIValidatorHTML do not depend on that. Effective exposure depends on the deployment's Shiro configuration/proxy setup, which is external to this snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Read/inspected: repository root build files and module layout; Apache Jena 5.5.0-SNAPSHOT main sources in jena-fuseki2 (core, main, access, webapp, UI JS/config, mod-geosparql), jena-arq HTTP/SPARQL execution and SERVICE handling, RDF/XML TripleX/StAX/TriX/SPARQL-XML parsing entry points, jena-core XML utilities and RDF/XML (ARP/RRX) readers, jena-langtag, jena-base I/O and logging helpers, selected jena-text, jena-geosparql, jena-tdb/jena-db, jena-shacl/jena-shex, jena-cmds and jena-permissions files. Searched broadly for command execution, deserialization, XML parser construction/hardening, path handling, request-parameter flows, HTML output, and security checks. Not exhaustively reviewed: all 5,231 files (e.g., most of jena-tdb2/jena-db storage internals, reasoners, jena-iri/jena-iri3986 internals, benchmark/test-support code), and no test sources are present in the snapshot.
limitations: Snapshot contains no test directories and no git metadata, so upstream diffs/fix commits and intended behavior could not be compared.
No code was compiled or executed and no HTTP requests were made; all findings are static only.
Default Shiro configuration limits /$/validate/* to loopback, so remote exploitability of the XSS depends on deployment configuration/proxying that cannot be verified from source alone.
The JavaCC/Jena parse-error message contents were inferred from the parser code (TokenMgrError/ParseException include the offending token image) but not verified at runtime.
Ruled-out leads (XXE in XML parsers, SERVICE default SSRF) may still contain subtleties in configurations/dependencies (e.g., Woodstox/Aalto on the classpath) that were not exercised.

rejected_leads.lead: Service.checkServiceAllowed/getBoolean ignores the 'symbol' argument and always reads httpServiceAllowed (jena-arq .../sparql/exec/http/Service.java lines 112-135).
rejected_leads.reason: Looks like a wrong-variable bug that makes the legacy/deprecated Service#serviceAllowed=false setting ineffective, so SERVICE could stay enabled (SSRF). Kept as a rejected lead because the documented current setting arq:httpServiceAllowed still works, so impact requires a legacy configuration and could not be confirmed as the intended flaw.

rejected_leads.lead: LangTagRFC5646 variant check uses a tautology: if (ch >= '0' || ch <= '9') at jena-langtag/.../LangTagRFC5646.java line 464, so 4-character variants not starting with a digit are accepted; also a dead 'new HashSet<>();' at line 485.
rejected_leads.reason: Real input-validation defect, but the practical security impact is low (acceptance of syntactically invalid language tags); rejected as the single strongest candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLLiteralType parses rdf:XMLLiteral lexical forms with a DocumentBuilderFactory hardened only with FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING (jena-core/.../util/JenaXMLInput.java lines 200-206; datatypes/xsd/impl/XMLLiteralType.java lines 127-148).
rejected_leads.reason: Static CWE-611 pattern; however the lexical form is wrapped as <xml-literal-fragment>...</xml-literal-fragment> before parsing, so a DOCTYPE/entity declaration cannot be injected ahead of the root element; no exploitable XXE path identified. Other RDF/XML, TriX and SPARQL-XML paths use JenaXMLInput/SysRRX with external DTD/entity features disabled.

rejected_leads.lead: FMod_Shiro declares unused defaultIniFileLocations/iniFileLocations and installs the Shiro filter only when --shiro or FUSEKI_SHIRO is set (jena-fuseki-main/.../mod/shiro/FMod_Shiro.java lines 78-137).
rejected_leads.reason: Suggests a removed fallback lookup, but in the standard server FMod_Admin/FusekiServerCtl.setup() copies the default shiro.ini into FUSEKI_BASE and sets FUSEKI_SHIRO before FMod_Shiro.prepare runs, so no missing-filter condition was demonstrated; treated as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: HttpAction.getInputStreamOneTime decodes Content-Encoding: deflate with DeflaterInputStream instead of InflaterInputStream (jena-fuseki-core/.../servlets/HttpAction.java lines 822-834).
rejected_leads.reason: Likely functional defect (request decompression), no clear security impact established.

summary: Repository: Apache Jena snapshot at version 5.5.0-SNAPSHOT (post-5.4.0, ~June 2025), 5,231 readable main-source files. I reviewed the HTTP-facing Fuseki modules (core, main, access, webapp, UI, geosparql module), ARQ query/update/service execution, RDF/XML and StAX/TriX parsing paths, jena-core XML utilities, jena-langtag, jena-base I/O, jena-text/jena-geosparql selected paths, and the project build/module layout. The strongest concrete issue I found is a reflected XSS class in the Fuseki HTML "validator" endpoints: request parameters and parser/validator error messages are written directly into a text/html response without output encoding, and the local `htmlQuote` helper is not applied on those paths. Other anomalies (SERVICE allow/deny comparison bug, language-tag validation tautology, unused Shiro default-ini fields, unhardened DOM factory in XMLLiteral parsing) were treated as unconfirmed/rejected leads and are listed below.
